# SOP Audit: The Forge, Belfast

**Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding** – first 7 days critical; no documented sequence for induction, movement screening, goal-setting, or coach assignment
- **Member Checkins** – no cadence for re-engagement post-signup (week 1, month 1, month 3); risk of silent churn
- **Cancellation & Churn** – no win-back protocol, exit interview process, or data capture on why members leave

- **Referral Programme** – no mechanics: incentive tier, redemption, tracking, or staff commission/bonus rules
- **Member Data Privacy & GDPR** – no data handling, consent, retention, or breach response documented
- **Troubleshooting Guide** – no decision tree for common member complaints (billing, coach issues, class booking, injury concerns)
- **Coaching Development Roadmap** – no progression framework, certification pathways, or performance review cadence
- **Class Quality Audit Checklist** – no monthly/quarterly standard-setting or peer/manager observation protocol

- **Weekly Key Coach Tasks** – likely missing: session prep checklists, admin handoffs, member communication templates, injury/incident logging

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**1. Audit what you're ACTUALLY selling right now**
- Have your coaches list every service they deliver (group classes, 1:1 coaching, nutrition checks, form assessments, etc.) — don't assume you know
- Note what members are currently paying for vs. what's bundled/free — this reveals pricing confusion
- **Do this in 2 hours with your head coach before designing anything**

**2. Build two separate menus — don't mix them**
- **Coach menu**: Service tiers by time/complexity (e.g., "30-min form check £25" vs. "12-week strength program £400") — coaches need to know what they're selling and what margin it covers
- **Member menu**: Stripped down, benefit-focused (e.g., "Unlimited classes + monthly 1:1 £65" not "coaching, programming, technique review") — members buy outcomes, not features

**3. Price from your margin backwards**
- Calculate: what does 1 hour of coach time cost you (salary + overhead)?
- Price so that selling 15 hours/week of 1:1 work covers that coach's full cost + profit margin
- **If you can't hit margin targets, bundle services differently — don't just cut price**

**4. Test with your best 5 members first**
- Send them the draft menu before launch; get feedback on clarity
- Watch if they ask questions — if they do, rewrite that section
- **Launch next week, not after endless rounds of internal debate**

**5. Make it a live doc on your website + printed in gym**
- URL: theforgegym.

# The Forge — Fractional CFO Analysis & Actions

## REVENUE — URGENT PRIORITY

**Revenue trend is volatile and declining. Last 3 months (Jul–Sep avg £19,313) vs prior 3 (Apr–Jun avg £16,232) show +19% growth, BUT September's £22,016 is an outlier; Aug dipped to £16,160 (lowest since relocation). Member count is up 36% (120→165) but revenue-per-member has collapsed from £139 (Apr) to £106 (Aug) — a red flag.**

- **Pricing audit now.** You're adding members but not collecting enough per head. Aug at £106/member suggests either discounts offered at relocation, free trial cohort not converting, or package mix shift to cheaper tiers. Audit current pricing tiers and trial-to-paid conversion rate. Target: return to £130+ revenue/member by November through tier repositioning or upsell (see below).

- **Class-fill analysis & premium add-ons.** With 165 members, identify which class times run <70% capacity. Run off-peak incentive pricing (early-bird rates) or shift marketing spend to promote quiet slots. *Simultaneously*, launch add-ons: nutrition coaching packages (£30–50/month retainer), personal training blocks (£15–25/session sold in bundles of 5), or merchandise/supplements (15–20% margin). Target: +£2,000/month from add-ons by end-Q4.

- **Churn spike in May (12.8%) + consistent 5–8% monthly.** That's your leak. Implement exit interviews (TeamUp has this) to tag reasons. Women-only fitness often churns on: class schedule, community feel, or price sensitivity post-relocation. Launch a "member win-back" campaign for lapsed members + a referral bonus (£20 credit per new member referred). Target: drop churn to <4% by Q1 2027.

## EXPENSES — LIKELY LEVER (DATA GAPS NOTED)

**You've given revenue but not P&L detail. Without wage bills, rent, and utilities, I'm reasoning from member count + space expansion.**

- **Staffing ratio check.** You moved to a bigger studio and added 45 members (120→165). If you haven't added instructors proportionally, you've likely improved per-member wage cost. If you *have* added staff, ensure utilisation: can they cover reception + classes + cleaning, or are hours bloated? Request a staff cost % of revenue; target 25–30% for a boutique gym
